issues.title: toJSONSchema emits non-standard format values ("includes", "starts_with", "ends_with") since 4.6.0
issues.body:
Since zod 4.6.0 (#6554, "derive JSON Schema constraints by folding checks in the converter"), `z.toJSONSchema` copies every `string_format` check's `format` name into the JSON Schema `format` keyword. For `.includes()`, `.startsWith()`, and `.endsWith()` that name is not a JSON Schema format, so validators such as ajv report `unknown format "includes" ignored`.

Reproduction on zod 4.6.5 (bun 1.4):

```ts
import { z } from "zod";
for (const [name, schema] of [
  ["includes", z.string().includes("x")],
  ["startsWith", z.string().startsWith("x")],
  ["endsWith", z.string().endsWith("x")],
]) console.log(name, JSON.stringify(z.toJSONSchema(schema)));
```

Output:

```text
includes {"$schema":"https://json-schema.org/draft/2020-12/schema","type":"string","format":"includes","pattern":"x"}
startsWith {"$schema":"https://json-schema.org/draft/2020-12/schema","type":"string","format":"starts_with","pattern":"^x.*"}
endsWith {"$schema":"https://json-schema.org/draft/2020-12/schema","type":"string","format":"ends_with","pattern":".*x$"}
```

On 4.5.4 the same schemas emit only the `pattern`. Expected: the `pattern` alone, since it already carries the constraint, and `format` only for names JSON Schema (or zod's documented format set) defines.

Where it comes from: `json-schema-processors` copies `def.format` from every `string_format` check, and `_includes`/`_startsWith`/`_endsWith` construct their checks with `check: "string_format"` and the internal names above.

## Fix

Branch, ready to open as a PR by a collaborator (this repository refuses PR creation from my account):

https://github.com/colinhacks/zod/compare/main...Vivswan:zod:fix/json-schema-string-format-trait

```text
                  main                                                      branch
includes          {"type":"string","format":"includes","pattern":"x"}       {"type":"string","pattern":"x"}
url().startsWith  {"type":"string","format":"starts_with","pattern":"^x.*"} {"type":"string","format":"uri","pattern":"^x.*"}
```

- **One change** in `json-schema-processors.ts`: a `string_format` check contributes a `format` only if it carries the `$ZodCheckStringFormat` trait.
- **Why that works:** `includes`, `startsWith` and `endsWith` are built with `$ZodCheck.init`, not `$ZodCheckStringFormat.init`. That is why they never wrote `bag.format` on 4.5.x.
- **Test:** fails on `main` with `"format": "includes"` received, passes on the branch. Full suite green.
- **Bundle:** unchanged unless `toJSONSchema` is used, then +31 gzip bytes classic, +30 mini.
- **Trait read, not `instanceof`:** `instanceof` pulls `$ZodCheckStringFormat` into mini bundles that never build a format check (+89 bytes).
issues.author: Vivswan

comments.body:
PR creation is limited to collaborators here, so sharing the fix as a branch: https://github.com/colinhacks/zod/compare/main...MFA-G:zod:fix/json-schema-pattern-formats

The `string_format` contributor in the JSON Schema converter now skips `includes`, `starts_with` and `ends_with` when choosing the format, so those checks emit only their `pattern` like they did on 4.5.x. A real format next to them (`z.email().startsWith("a")`) is still emitted, and `lowercase`/`uppercase` are unchanged since they already emitted a format before #6554. One added test covers all three and the combined case; it fails on `main` and passes on the branch, and the full vitest suite, biome and `check:comments` pass.

comments.body: Your analysis shows json-schema-processors copies def.format, causing the unexpected 'includes' format in Zod 4.6.5, whereas 4.5.4 emitted only the pattern. Such schema drift mirrors the challenges of aligning loosely defined APIs with formal contracts like [Mobile Government Services](https://inmate-search.mobilecountyal.org/) Your ready PR that removes the non‑standard format and keeps only the regex pattern should appease ajv and restore proper validation. Including a test that asserts only the pattern key exists will give future contributors a clear safety net.
comments.author: kanedavid56

comments.body:
Hi everyone,

I’ve worked on a fix for this issue and wanted to share the implementation and testing details here for review.

The problem appears when `z.toJSONSchema()` processes string constraints created with `includes()`, `startsWith()`, and `endsWith()`. These constraints can emit internal check names such as `includes`, `starts_with`, and `ends_with` as JSON Schema `format` values. These are not standard format values, and the constraints already have regex pattern representations.

### What I changed

I updated the string-format processing logic in `packages/zod/src/v4/core/json-schema-processors.ts` to emit a `format` property only when the check has the `$ZodCheckStringFormat` trait.

This allows genuine string-format checks to keep emitting their supported formats while preventing substring constraints from introducing non-standard ones. The existing pattern generation remains unchanged.

I kept the change intentionally small and avoided importing concrete check classes or relying on `instanceof`. The implementation uses the existing trait information to distinguish actual string-format checks from other checks that share the same internal check identifier.

### Regression tests

I added coverage in `packages/zod/src/v4/classic/tests/to-json-schema.test.ts` for the following cases:

- `includes()` generates its pattern without emitting `format: "includes"`.
- `startsWith()` generates its pattern without emitting `format: "starts_with"`.
- `endsWith()` generates its pattern without emitting `format: "ends_with"`.
- Existing formats such as `uri`, `email`, and `uuid` are preserved.
- Chaining `.url().startsWith("https://")` preserves `format: "uri"` rather than allowing the later constraint to overwrite it.

### Validation

I ran the focused regression tests and the relevant JSON Schema test suites:

- Focused regression tests: **12 passed**.
- `to-json-schema.test.ts`: **513 passed**.
- `to-json-schema-methods.test.ts`: **267 passed**.
- Type-checking reported no errors in these runs.
- `git diff --check` completed without whitespace errors.

### Implementation and review

The changes are available in my fork's pull request:

https://github.com/giteshchaudhari681-art/zod/pull/1

The contribution contains two commits: one for the regression tests and one for the production fix.

I was unable to create a pull request directly against this repository because GitHub restricted PR creation from my account. I’m sharing the work here so it can still be considered for upstream review.

Could a maintainer please take a look at the linked changes and let me know if anything should be adjusted before they can be accepted?

Thank you for your time and for maintaining Zod.
comments.author: giteshchaudhari681-art

issues.title: Rollup tries to interpret references to `@__PURE__` annotations in Zod's comments
issues.body:
Hello, using either Zod `4.6.5` or `4.5.4`, the following warnings appear during vite build that did not appear when building with Zod `4.3.5`:

```md
[info] vite v5.4.3 building for production...
[info] transforming...

node_modules/zod/v4/core/util.js (400:0): A comment
"// Wrapped in a `@__PURE__` IIFE: esbuild never tree-shakes a top-level initializer that contains a member access on `Number`, so the bare object literal survived into every bundle."
in "node_modules/zod/v4/core/util.js" contains an annotation that Rollup cannot interpret due to the position of the comment. The comment will be removed to avoid issues.

node_modules/zod/v4/core/regexes.js (74:0): A comment
"/** Anchors a pattern source. The interpolation lives here rather than at the call site because
 * esbuild will not drop a `@__PURE__` call whose own argument interpolates a variable, but it
 * will drop `anchor(dateSource)`. Keeping it inline pinned `date` into every bundle. */"
in "node_modules/zod/v4/core/regexes.js" contains an annotation that Rollup cannot interpret due to the position of the comment. The comment will be removed to avoid issues.

[info] ✓ 3679 modules transformed.
```

Rollup is trying to interpret references to bundler annotations in these comments as actual annotations, correctly failing to do so as they are not, but still emitting warnings.

Would it be possible to avoid including these annotations in comments or otherwise address it in Zod? Or should this be addressed or configured to be ignored on the bundler side?
issues.author: audibleptr

comments.body:

Detailed triage and the implementation plan are in `.triage/issues/6619/results.md`.
